estimation_sources.env:VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND: vllm/distributed/device_communicators/flashinfer_all_reduce.py:143-178@5df63a72 resolves an unset (auto) backend to mnnvl, with a trtllm fallback allowed, on one node, and to mnnvl without fallback on compute capability 10.0 and up across nodes, so a recipe that states mnnvl across nodes on such a part runs as the default does, while one that states it on one node does not (no fallback); the latency kernel prices every tensor-parallel all-reduce from the NCCL sweep whichever FlashInfer backend runs (it has no implementation-keyed all-reduce entry), so the stand-in changes no price. The field's valid_when says for which values and groups the stand-in is exact; fields/stand_in_vectors.json holds it to _resolve_fi_ar_backend; a single-node group on compute capability 10.0 and up is exact under the assumption that the node has NVSwitch multicast (a stated mnnvl on a node without it disables the FlashInfer all-reduce, auto falls back to trtllm, flashinfer_all_reduce.py:196-232@4ba787ec), true of every Blackwell part in the catalog (owner _resolve_fi_ar_backend+multicast)
estimation_sources.env:UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED: vllm/distributed/nixl_utils.py:20-36@5df63a72 sets UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED to 1024 itself when the environment does not state it, so a run that states 1024 runs as an unset one does; UCX's variable (src/ucs/memory/rcache.c:114-118 at UCX v1.19.0, the version inside the nixl 1.5.0 wheel is not known) only sets when invalidated registration regions are cleaned up and does not choose a transport or a rate; the field's valid_when says for which values the stand-in is exact; fields/stand_in_vectors.json holds it to _maybe_set_ucx_rcache_limit
estimation_sources.env:UCX_TLS: NIXL's UCX backend is the default (vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py:525-526@5df63a72) and UCX_TLS restricts the transports it may use (UCX FAQ). The engine prices a handoff between nodes over the NIC at the cluster fabric's rate unless UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL=y is stated (core/kernelmodel, rackHandoff), which is the path a list of RDMA transports without cuda_ipc takes, so unset stands in exactly for such a list; the field's valid_when says for which lists the stand-in is exact
estimation_sources.env:NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE: vLLM's serving process does not read NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE (it names it only in vllm/distributed/weight_transfer/sharded_rdt_trainer.py:1156@4ba787ec); NCCL does. NCCL autodetects cuMem since 2.19 and the variable only overrides that, so a stated 1 on a run that completed is NCCL's default and the unset stand-in is exact for it; a stated 0 disables cuMem (and with it NVLS and MNNVL), changes the buffers NCCL registers, and is not exact. The field's valid_when says for which values; fields/stand_in_vectors.json holds it (owner nccl-user-guide)
estimation_sources.env:NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE: vLLM's serving process does not read NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE (it names it only in vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py:1409@4ba787ec, where it sets 0); NCCL does. The default is 2 and 1 differs from it only in making a failed NVLS allocation fatal (NCCL user guide), so a stated 1 or 2 on a run that completed runs as the unset stand-in does; 0 disables NVLink SHARP, which changes the collectives' algorithm, and is not exact. The field's valid_when says for which values; fields/stand_in_vectors.json holds it (owner nccl-user-guide)
estimation_sources.env:VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_MXFP4_MXFP8: vLLM v0.33.0 does not read VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_MXFP4_MXFP8; v0.22.0 did (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py at v0.22.0, lines 501-509: a set value forces FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8 with a dynamic MXFP8 activation). It was deprecated in 9b54e50e2 (vllm-project/vllm#43148, 2026-05-21) and removed in v0.24.0 by 03878d1c2 (vllm-project/vllm#44992, 2026-06-11, 'Deprecations for v0.23 and v0.24'; v0.23.0 still lists it as deprecated). At vLLM 4ba787ec the same selection is --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm with quantization_config.moe.activation mxfp8: map_mxfp4_backend gives the BF16 and MXFP8 variants and _filter_by_activation keeps the MXFP8 one (fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py:361-364, :614-631); its kernel needs compute capability family 10 (experts/trtllm_mxfp4_moe.py:121-123).
estimation_sources.env:VLLM_MXFP4_USE_MARLIN: vLLM v0.33.0 does not read VLLM_MXFP4_USE_MARLIN; v0.22.0 did (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py at v0.22.0, line 526 for the MoE, and kernels/linear/__init__.py:736 for the MXFP4 linear kernel: a set value forces Marlin). It was deprecated in 9b54e50e2 (vllm-project/vllm#43148, 2026-05-21) and removed in v0.24.0 by 03878d1c2 (vllm-project/vllm#44992, 2026-06-11, 'Deprecations for v0.23 and v0.24'; v0.23.0 still lists it as deprecated). At vLLM 4ba787ec the MoE selection is --moe-backend marlin (fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py:378, :675-710; MarlinExperts needs compute capability 7.5 or more, experts/marlin_moe.py:592-594) and the linear one is --linear-backend marlin; a model with no MXFP4 linear layer (gpt-oss-120b keeps its attention in bf16) is unaffected by the linear half.
estimation_sources.env:DYN_REQUEST_PLANE_CODEC: Dynamo's runtime, not vLLM's serving process, reads DYN_REQUEST_PLANE_CODEC (lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network.rs:130-136 at ai-dynamo/dynamo 807aaaa0, 2026-11-18; docs architecture.md:77: the variable selects msgpack or json and the endpoint advertises its codec). from_config_value maps None, empty and msgpack to Msgpack and json to Json, so a stated msgpack is the unset choice at that commit; the image's Dynamo release is not recorded, and an earlier release whose unset choice was json would make the stand-in differ by the encoding cost only. The field's valid_when holds msgpack alone
estimation_sources.env:NCCL_P2P_LEVEL: vLLM's serving process does not read NCCL_P2P_LEVEL; NCCL does (ncclGetUserP2pLevel, src/graph/paths.cc:309-313 at NVIDIA/nccl v2.32.6-1 ad2d192c). The level only removes P2P between GPU pairs whose path type is above it, so on Blackwell parts (compute capability 10.x: HGX B200/B300 and the GB200/GB300 NVL72 trays, NVSwitch between all GPUs of a node and between nodes of a rack with multi-node NVLink) a stated NVL is the default. The field's valid_when holds NVL on compute capability 10.x only: on a PCIe or NVLink-bridge part it would forbid P2P the default allows. The NCCL version inside the images is not recorded
estimation_sources.env:NCCL_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT: NCCL_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT has no reader in NVIDIA/nccl v2.32.6-1 (ad2d192c), PyTorch v2.11.0 (torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp and ProcessGroupNCCL.hpp) or vLLM v0.33.0 (4ba787ec), searched by name on 2026-11-18. The libraries inside the images are not recorded, and a reader this search did not reach would make the stand-in differ in a failure-detection timeout only, which a run that completed did not exercise. The field's valid_when holds the one value the corpus states, 1800
estimation_sources.env:TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC: PyTorch reads TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC (torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:1709 and ProcessGroupNCCL.hpp:96-105 at v2.11.0); vLLM's serving process does not name it. The field's valid_when holds the one value the corpus states, 1800
estimation_sources.env:TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: vLLM v0.33.0 names TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST only in collect_env (excluded: a separate command) and in its ep_kernels README; PyTorch reads it (torch/utils/cpp_extension.py:2579 at v2.11.0). Unset, the arch list is the visible devices' capabilities (:2582-2590), so a stated list equal to the device's capability is the same build. The field's valid_when holds 10.0 on a part of compute capability 10.0 (B200, GB200) and 9.0 on a part of compute capability 9.0 (H100, H200); another list or part is not shown to match
estimation_sources.env:UCX_MAX_RMA_RAILS: vLLM's serving process does not read UCX_MAX_RMA_RAILS; UCX does (src/ucp/core/ucp_context.c:233-235 at openucx/ucx v1.19.0 e4636149: default "1", the maximal number of devices an RMA operation may use in parallel). NIXL's UCX backend moves KV with RMA operations (ai-dynamo/nixl 684ca383 src/plugins/ucx/ucx_utils.cpp:292 and :317 (ucp_get_nbx and ucp_put_nbx carry a transfer; ucp_am_send_nbx at :259 carries the notification)). The UCX version inside the nixl wheel is not recorded. The field's valid_when holds 1
estimation_sources.env:UCX_MAX_RNDV_RAILS: vLLM's serving process does not read UCX_MAX_RNDV_RAILS; UCX does (src/ucp/core/ucp_context.c:226-228 at openucx/ucx v1.19.0 e4636149: default "2", the devices a rendezvous operation may use in parallel). The KV bytes travel as RMA (ucp_get_nbx at ucx_utils.cpp:292 and ucp_put_nbx at :317, ai-dynamo/nixl 684ca383 src/plugins/ucx/ucx_utils.cpp:292 and :317 (ucp_get_nbx and ucp_put_nbx carry a transfer; ucp_am_send_nbx at :259 carries the notification)), so the value does not reach them; a UCX build in which an RMA operation of that size ran as a rendezvous would differ. The field's valid_when holds 1
estimation_sources.env:UCX_RNDV_SCHEME: vLLM's serving process does not read UCX_RNDV_SCHEME; UCX does (src/ucp/core/ucp_context.c:246-252 at openucx/ucx v1.19.0 e4636149). The KV bytes travel as RMA (ai-dynamo/nixl 684ca383 src/plugins/ucx/ucx_utils.cpp:292 and :317 (ucp_get_nbx and ucp_put_nbx carry a transfer; ucp_am_send_nbx at :259 carries the notification)), so the rendezvous scheme does not reach them; the same caveat as UCX_MAX_RNDV_RAILS applies. The field's valid_when holds put_zcopy
estimation_sources.env:UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE: vLLM sets UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n itself on XPU, because the cache can misdetect GPU memory as host memory (vllm/platforms/xpu.py:455-459@4ba787ec), and UCX documents the option as the switch for the memory type cache (openucx/ucx v1.19.0 e4636149). On a CUDA part a stated n differs from the default try by a driver query per address range, a per-operation CPU cost that the engine does not price for either value (the same standing as UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED). The field's valid_when holds n
estimation_sources.env:UCX_MEMTYPE_REG_WHOLE: UCX has MEMTYPE_REG_WHOLE_ALLOC_TYPES (src/ucp/core/ucp_context.c:163 at openucx/ucx v1.19.0 e4636149, the same name in v1.15.0, v1.17.0, v1.18.0 and v1.20.0) and no option called MEMTYPE_REG_WHOLE; vLLM names neither. A UCX that reads the shorter name would differ in which allocations it registers whole, a registration cost and not a rate; none of the five tags checked does. The field's valid_when holds n
estimation_sources.env:TILELANG_CLEANUP_TEMP_FILES: vllm/env_override.py:183@4ba787ec is os.environ.setdefault("TILELANG_CLEANUP_TEMP_FILES", "1"): the variable's value in the serving process is 1 whether or not the run stated it. TileLang reads it to delete its compile-time temporary files. The field's valid_when holds 1

estimation_sources.env:VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL: vLLM v0.33.0 reads envs.VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL at llm_engine.py:467 (do_log_stats_with_interval) and server_utils.py:83 and grpc_server.py:139 (the forced-log loops), and nowhere else outside benchmarks. approximates.evidence: the registry prices a routed expert group by weight format on the ramp fitted for it (blis-substrate#150, #285), and records that the stated backend is not the one it measured
approximates.differs: a stated backend (FlashInfer TRT-LLM, CUTLASS or CuteDSL, DeepGEMM mega-MoE, Marlin, or Triton) runs its own kernel with its own ramp; the experts are priced as the engine resolves the field when it is unset, so the step carries that backend's difference. On an SM90 part with block-FP8 experts the engine prices a stated Triton or FlashInfer CUTLASS backend from its own lane (the plan states the kernel, lowering expertsKernel); the point is still carried as this substitution because the unset field resolves Triton at expert-parallel width 1 and FlashInfer CUTLASS above it, so a stated backend that is not that one is priced from the other's lane. A stated marlin on an SM90 part with MXFP4 experts is the kernel the engine already prices: a part with no four-bit peak prices MXFP4 grouped routed experts as vLLM's Marlin W4A16 grouped GEMM on the registry's w4a16_mxfp4_grouped ramp (blis-substrate kernel formatFit; registry fit_marlin_grouped_ramp.py), while the unset field resolves Triton for gpt-oss on SM90 (oracle/mxfp4.py _get_priority_backends_for_gpt_oss, TRITON before MARLIN, vllm@4ba787ec). The SM90 clause is valid for block-FP8 experts (Triton, FlashInfer CUTLASS) and for MXFP4 experts (Marlin) only; the clause grammar cannot test the weight scheme (inference-sim/blis-substrate#384), and the corpus has no other SM90 recipe that states any of these backends

estimation.preserves: the engine's pricing: BLIS hosts no Dynamo request plane (the router is a stand-in), so the codec that encodes each request message between a Dynamo frontend and its workers has no component here to act on, and msgpack is the codec Dynamo selects when the variable is unset or empty (from_config_value, lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network.rs:132-152 at ai-dynamo/dynamo 807aaaa0). A stated json differs only in the encoding cost of each message, which is part of the frontend overhead neither value is priced for

NCCL's own choice: since NCCL 2.19 it allocates with the CUDA cuMem functions whenever the system supports them (NCCL user guide, NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE), and a stated 1 only overrides the autodetection with the same choice. The latency kernel prices every collective from the NCCL sweep at NCCL's defaults

NCCL's own choice: the default is 2, use multi-node NVLink where the system supports it and fall back to the network where it does not, and 1 differs only in failing communicator initialization when MNNVL is unsupported or cannot be enabled (NCCL user guide, NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE), which a run that completed did not do. The latency kernel prices every collective from the NCCL sweep at NCCL's defaults, and a stated cluster's NVLink domain is a catalog fact, not a setting

NCCL's own choice: the default is 2, use NVLink SHARP where the system supports it, and 1 differs only in failing communicator initialization when the NVLS resources cannot be allocated (NCCL user guide, NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE), which a run that completed did not do. The latency kernel prices every collective from the NCCL sweep at NCCL's defaults

NCCL's own choice on a part whose every GPU pair is joined by NVLink through NVSwitch: the path type between such GPUs is NVL, and NCCL allows P2P for a pair whose path type is no greater than the level (ncclTopoCheckP2p, src/graph/paths.cc:383-395 at NVIDIA/nccl v2.32.6-1 ad2d192c). The default level is PATH_PXB (paths.cc:383) and a stated NVL lowers it to PATH_NVL, so the two differ only for a pair whose path is NVB or farther, which a Blackwell HGX B200 or NVL72 node does not have. The latency kernel prices every collective from the NCCL sweep at NCCL's defaults

nothing: no source searched reads NCCL_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT, so a stated value and an unset one run alike. The variable is not one of NCCL's (no occurrence in NVIDIA/nccl v2.32.6-1 ad2d192c), PyTorch's ProcessGroupNCCL (v2.11.0 names TORCH_NCCL_* variables, not this) or vLLM's (v0.33.0 4ba787ec names it nowhere)
vLLM's own setting: vllm/env_override.py sets TILELANG_CLEANUP_TEMP_FILES to 1 itself when the environment does not state it (os.environ.setdefault), so a run that states 1 runs as an unset one does

the kernels the run used: TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST lists the compute capabilities torch.utils.cpp_extension compiles a JIT extension for, and unset it compiles for the visible GPUs (_get_cuda_arch_flags, torch/utils/cpp_extension.py:2577-2590 at pytorch v2.11.0), so on a part of capability 10.0 a stated 10.0, and on a part of capability 9.0 (H100, H200) a stated 9.0, builds for the architecture the device has. The kernels' rates come from the registry, which a compile flag does not change

a run that did not hang: PyTorch's NCCL heartbeat monitor aborts the process when the watchdog thread has not beaten for the timeout (default 8 minutes, getCvarInt(TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC, 60 * 8), ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:1709 at pytorch v2.11.0), and a stated 1800 differs from the default only in how long a stuck process is waited for before it is killed, which a run that completed never reached
UCX's own default: MAX_RMA_RAILS defaults to 1 (ucp_context_config_table, src/ucp/core/ucp_context.c:233 at openucx/ucx v1.19.0), so a stated 1 is the unset value

the rate a KV transfer runs at: NIXL's UCX backend moves KV with ucp_get_nbx and ucp_put_nbx, RMA operations whose lanes MAX_RMA_RAILS bounds, not a rendezvous, and MAX_RNDV_RAILS (default 2) bounds the devices a rendezvous uses (src/ucp/core/ucp_context.c:226-228 at openucx/ucx v1.19.0 e4636149); the notification NIXL sends is an active message of a few bytes, below any rendezvous threshold

the transport and the rate: the memory type cache stores which address ranges are GPU memory so a lookup need not ask the driver (src/ucs/memory/memtype_cache.c, ucs_memtype_cache_lookup at :324; the option is src/ucs/config/global_opts.c:167-169 at openucx/ucx v1.19.0 e4636149, default try), and turning it off makes UCX ask the driver for each address; it does not choose a transport or change a rate

nothing: UCX has no option of this name, so a stated value is read by no code and only draws a warning that the variable is unused (ucs_config_parser warns 'unused environment variable', src/ucs/config/parser.c:2359 at openucx/ucx v1.19.0 e4636149)
the value vLLM sets itself when the environment does not state one (nixl_utils.py:20-36@5df63a72)

the rate a KV transfer runs at: RNDV_SCHEME chooses how a rendezvous moves its payload (default auto; get_zcopy, put_zcopy, the pipelined schemes and rkey_ptr, src/ucp/core/ucp_context.c:246-252 at openucx/ucx v1.19.0 e4636149), and NIXL's UCX backend moves KV with RMA operations, not a rendezvous

the NIC path the engine prices for a handoff between nodes when UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL=y is not stated (core/kernelmodel): a transport list that names an RDMA transport, or all, reaches the NIC; a deny list or a list with no RDMA transport does not. UCX FAQ for the list syntax; no vLLM function resolves it

estimation.preserves: the backend vLLM's _resolve_fi_ar_backend picks for the tensor-parallel group (flashinfer_all_reduce.py:143-178@5df63a72). One node: auto picks mnnvl with a trtllm fallback when the multicast workspace cannot be created, and a stated mnnvl picks mnnvl with no fallback, so the two differ on a node without NVSwitch multicast, which the stand-in cannot be told. On compute capability 10.0 and up every node the recorded runs used has NVSwitch multicast (HGX B200 and B300, the GB200 and GB300 NVL72 trays), the fallback is never taken, and a stated mnnvl on one node is exact under that assumption, which the point's estimation text states; on a lower capability it is not exact. Several nodes: auto picks mnnvl without fallback on compute capability 10.0 and up, and turns FlashInfer all-reduce off below it.
